To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the size-scale effects in ductile fracture can be explained by the competition between the two basic forms of non-linearities: elasto- plasticity inside the grains (which is responsible for hardening) and classic cohesive cracking at the grain boundaries (which is responsible of softening).

the size-scale effects in ductile fracture of polycrystals can be predicted and explained by using the same strategy that has been used successfully to predict the size-scale effects of quasi-brittles, namely a global constitutive model for the undamaged part of the material and a cohesive crack model with damage for the cracking part.
the shape of the global hardening cohesive zone constitutive model can be deduced by mesoscale numerical simulations of polychristalline metals.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the study of the influence of microstructure on ductile failure of polycrystals and with the derivation of a macro-scale constitutive relation that can be used to simulate the mechanical behavior of ductile materials.
a multi-scale computational strategy to predict the size-scale effects in the mechanical response of polycrystals undergoing plastic deformation and ductile fracture.

the development of a numerical method to predict the mechanical behavior of polycrystaline ductile metals under tension, where the size-scale effects are taken into account by using the hardening cohesive zone method.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the shape of the hardening cohesive zone law is a result of the inter-play between the elasto-plastic behaviour at the grain scale and the cohesive behaviour at the grain boundary.
a hardening cohesive zone is a meso-scale effect that can be observed at the macro-scale in the form of a softening constitutive relation.
the shape of the constitutive curve for ductile fracture is the result of a complex interplay between the elasto-plastic behaviour of the material and the cracking process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

The main takeaway from our work is that
the shape of the global constitutive law is not only a function of the microstructural parameters but also of the meso-scale boundary conditions and of the meso-macro scale transition rules.

a cohesive zone model with softening, which can be used at the macro scale, can be obtained by considering the interplay between elasto-plastic deformation inside the grains and cohesive cracking along the grain boundaries.

a global constitutive model for ductile fracture, which is able to reproduce the size-scale effects in the mechanical response of metals, can be deduce by a simple combination of two basic nonlinearities: elastically-plastic behavior of grains and cohesive cracking of grain boundaries.
